clue.text: Young child given small railway and soldiers

parts.note: a young child is an infant
RY is the short form of railway

explanation.surface: A toddler is handed a model train set and some toy soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantry are foot troops, the army's soldiers who fight on foot.

clue.text: Overrun with finest jumble

indicators.note: to jumble the word finest is to mix its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Something is swamped by a heap of the best things all mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: To infest a place is to swarm over it, as pests overrun a house.

clue.text: Unhampered, bicycle makes coast

parts.note: unhampered means free
a wheel is informal for a bicycle, as in going for a spin on your wheels

explanation.surface: Unencumbered, a cyclist glides along the seashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coast' looks like the seaside; it is the verb, to roll without pedalling.
explanation.definitionFit: To freewheel is to roll along without pedalling, which is to coast downhill.

clue.text: Lowest emotional state rainstorm about break of day

indicators.note: about here means placed around another letter
storm in the run-together word signals that the letters of rain are thrown about
the break of day is its very start, so its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone at rock bottom watches a downpour at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rainstorm' is read as RAIN plus 'storm', the anagram signal: NAIR goes about D, the first letter of 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, here a person's deepest low.

clue.text: Spring lock

parts.note: read not as a latch but as a lock of hair that curls like a coiled spring

explanation.surface: A locksmith's term for a latch that snaps shut.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a tight curl of hair, a springy lock.

clue.text: Lap-dancing circle needs doctor with composure

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so lap is rearranged

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A club performer in a ring of admirers calls for a medic, yet stays cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assured poise, calm confidence under pressure.

clue.text: Simple row can bring one to court

parts.note: simple means plain
a row, a quarrel, is a tiff

explanation.surface: A trivial quarrel ends up in a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who sues, taking another person before a judge.

clue.text: The Way of the World

parts.note: read not as Congreve's play or worldly custom but as the path the Earth travels round the Sun

explanation.surface: The title of a Restoration comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is the curved path a planet takes around its star.

clue.text: News round at home

parts.note: a round of ammunition is a bullet
at home means in

explanation.surface: A report of shots fired near a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short report of the latest news.

clue.text: Was he never an "in" writer?

parts.note: in cricket the side out in the field is never the side in to bat, so a writer named after that activity was never in

explanation.surface: A question whether some author was ever fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Fielding wrote Tom Jones; in cricket the team fielding is never 'in' (batting).
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fielding was the 18th-century English novelist of Tom Jones, and fielding is the cricket side not batting.

clue.text: Spring doctor in prison

indicators.note: in places the doctor inside the prison

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail, a prison
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor locked up behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: To gambol is to leap about playfully, to skip and bound.

clue.text: Something of an industrious group

indicators.note: something of a word is a part of it, so the answer sits inside the next word

explanation.surface: A busy, hardworking team.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a set of three, a small group or band.

clue.text: Broadcaster worse after treatment

indicators.note: after treatment the word worse has been worked on, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A radio presenter's health declines after medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcaster' is not a presenter: broadcasting is scattering seed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer scattering seed broadcasts it, so one who scatters seed is a broadcaster.

clue.text: Operatic spectacles put on by Handel, we hear

definitions.text: Operatic spectacles put on by Handel, we hear

parts.words: Operatic spectacles put on by Handel, we hear
parts.note: read not as staged operas by the composer but as glasses for the opera held up by a handle, the composer's name sounding like that word

explanation.surface: A review of the composer's lavish opera productions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handel' is said like 'handle': these opera glasses are held to the eyes by a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of opera glasses mounted on a long handle.

clue.text: Polecat, female, turning over ground in France

indicators.note: turning over means the French word is read backwards

parts.note: terre is French for ground or earth

explanation.surface: A female polecat digs over soil in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The ferret is the domesticated form of the polecat, a small weasel-like animal.

clue.text: Peter involved in vice, being susceptible

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A man called Peter is drawn into wickedness, being easily led.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles PETER together with VICE, nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Receptive means open to ideas or influence, ready to take things in.

clue.text: Working paper increases, say, in Japan

definitions.text: Working paper increases, say, in Japan

parts.words: Working paper increases, say, in Japan
parts.note: read not as an office document but as working sheets of paper into folds, the kind of word used for increases such as tenfold, a Japanese art

explanation.surface: A report on paper production rising in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'increases' are folds, as in twofold or tenfold.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into shapes.

clue.text: A talent, an unusual present while pregnant

indicators.note: presenting the letters in an unusual way means rearranging them

explanation.surface: An unexpected gift arrives during pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenatal means before birth, during the months of carrying a baby.

clue.text: Henry in rustic game

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the country dweller

parts.note: a rustic, a country dweller, is a peasant
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A countryman named Henry plays a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Game is wild birds shot for sport and food, and a pheasant is one.

clue.text: Fierce woman sending out the call

indicators.note: sending the words out of order means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: An angry woman is put out after being summoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A hellcat is a spiteful, violent-tempered woman, a virago.

clue.text: Powder found in hospital cabinets?

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A dusting powder kept in a hospital cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into a fine powder for the skin.

clue.text: Such a match is held on specially prepared surface

definitions.text: Such a match is held on specially prepared surface

parts.words: Such a match is held on specially prepared surface
parts.note: read not as a sports fixture on a groomed pitch but as a match that lights only when struck on the box's special strip

explanation.surface: A sports match played on a carefully tended pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety match ignites only when struck on the treated strip of its box.

clue.text: Drunken Caledonian losing key

indicators.note: losing means the letter is taken out

parts.note: Caledonia is the old Latin name for Scotland, so Caledonian means Scottish
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: A tipsy Scot has mislaid his house key.
explanation.definitionFit: Sottish means like a sot, a habitual drunkard, so fuddled with drink.

clue.text: One in cast of producer's first film

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word producer's

parts.note: a film, a thin coating, is a layer

explanation.surface: An actor appears in a producer's debut movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is an actor, one member of a cast.

clue.text: George not known in Lancaster?

parts.note: read not as a man unknown in a northern town but as the RAF nickname George for the automatic flying device, missing from a Lancaster bomber

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man named George is a stranger in Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' was RAF slang for the automatic pilot; the Lancaster was a Second World War bomber.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopilot steers an aircraft automatically, with no hand on the controls.

clue.text: Rotten time coming up for some soldiers

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rotten, of quality, means poor

explanation.surface: A bad time arrives for a body of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns POOR plus T into TROOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a unit of soldiers, such as a cavalry company.

clue.text: Commonplace to disqualify a learner-driver?

parts.note: to disqualify someone is to ban them
L is the plate shown by a learner-driver in Britain

explanation.surface: A dull everyday question about barring a learner from driving.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means trite and dull, utterly ordinary.

clue.text: One trapped in farm building is a child

indicators.note: trapped in means held inside the barn

parts.note: a barn is a farm building
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A youngster gets stuck in a barn.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is the Scottish and northern word for a child.

clue.text: Who's a pretty boy, then, at university?

definitions.text: Who's a pretty boy, then, at university?

parts.words: Who's a pretty boy, then, at university?
parts.note: read as a question whose reply about a pretty boy at a university sounds like a college lecturer being the one

explanation.surface: Cooing at a pet parrot, transplanted to a college.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as 'A don is': a don is a university lecturer, and Adonis was the beautiful youth of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the handsome youth loved by Aphrodite, so any very good-looking young man.

clue.text: Lots of revs make small cars go

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car, so minis are small cars
a go, an attempt, is a try

explanation.surface: A driver guns the engine of a tiny car to get it moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revs' are not engine turns but reverends, the clergy collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: The clergy as a body form the ministry, so many reverends together.

clue.text: Row about double parking of lorry

indicators.note: about means the row goes around the doubled letter

parts.note: a row of seats is a tier

indicators.note: double means the parking letter appears twice

explanation.surface: An argument over a truck parked in two spaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipper is a lorry whose body tilts to dump its load.

clue.text: Thriller writer whose characters are snuffed out?

definitions.text: Thriller writer whose characters are snuffed out?

parts.words: Thriller writer whose characters are snuffed out?
parts.note: read as a crime novelist killing off cast members, and also as a maker of candles whose products are put out

explanation.surface: A crime novelist who kills off the people in his books.
explanation.walkthrough: Raymond Chandler wrote hardboiled thrillers; a chandler makes candles, which are snuffed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler wrote The Big Sleep, and a chandler originally made and sold candles.
